content.text: I'll read the tokens.json to understand its structure, then create and run the audit script.
Now I'll create the audit script that uses `klar` to check WCAG AA compliance for each foreground token against the background:

input.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Extract background color from tokens.json
BG=$(jq -r '.background' tokens.json)

# WCAG AA threshold for body text
WCAG_AA_THRESHOLD=4.5

# Iterate through foreground tokens and check contrast
jq -r '.foreground | to_entries[] | "\(.key) \(.value)"' tokens.json | while read -r token_name token_color; do
  # Get contrast ratio using klar
  ratio=$(klar contrast "$token_color" "$BG" --json | jq -r '.ratio')

  # Check if it passes WCAG AA
  if (( $(echo "$ratio >= $WCAG_AA_THRESHOLD" | bc -l) )); then
    status="PASS"
  else
    status="FAIL"
  fi

  printf "%-15s %s (%.2f:1)\n" "$token_name" "$status" "$ratio"
done
